//| echo: false
buildQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">
    <button style="
      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;
      background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);
      color:#fff;border:none;padding:9px 22px;border-radius:50px;
      font-size:.95em;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
      box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45);
      transition:transform .15s,box-shadow .15s;"
      onmouseover="this.style.transform='scale(1.04)';this.style.boxShadow='0 5px 18px rgba(102,126,234,.55)'"
      onmouseout="this.style.transform='scale(1)';this.style.boxShadow='0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45)'"
    >
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(102,126,234,.12);color:#667eea;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide Quiz</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="2000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Stability of the Solar System

::: {.evidence-box}
### 🌑 Chapter 2.1: Stability of the Solar System

**PTO prompt:** Scientists think life may not have appeared until about **3.5 billion years ago** because it could not evolve during a time of instability in the solar system. Earth has relatively few impact craters, yet scientists believe it was constantly bombarded about **4 billion years ago**.

**Claim:** *Life did not appear until 3.5 billion years ago because the Earth was undergoing a period of heavy asteroid bombardment 4 billion years ago.*

**Key evidence:**

- **Moon rocks** brought back by Apollo include many impact melts dated to about **4.1–3.8 billion years ago**: the **late heavy bombardment**.
- The Moon has **no plate tectonics, weathering, erosion, or liquid water**, so its craters are preserved. Earth is the Moon's neighbor, so it must have been hit even harder.
- Earth has **few craters** (fewer than 200 confirmed impact structures) because plate tectonics, weathering, erosion, and volcanism **recycle and resurface** its crust.
- The oldest fossil evidence of life (microbial **stromatolites**) is about **3.5 billion years old**, after the bombardment.

**Strengths and limitations:** The Moon samples are directly dated, but they come from only a few landing sites. Earth has very few rocks older than 4 billion years, so its own record of the bombardment has been erased. Some scientists think the "late" bombardment was the tail end of a slow decline rather than a spike.

📖 Review the chapter: [Stability of the Solar System](unit2-solar-system.qmd)
:::

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: Stability of the Solar System explanation + Reflection (pp. 9–10)

In your explanation, include:

1. The **evidence for the late heavy bombardment** and the **time** it occurred
2. Why **Earth has relatively few impact craters**, citing evidence from the 5E activities
3. The evidence that **life appeared after** the late heavy bombardment
4. The **strengths or limitations** of this evidence

**Reflection:** for each piece of evidence, describe the **scientific concept and/or logical reasoning** that links it to the claim.
:::

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Coevolution of Earth and Life

::: {.evidence-box}
### 🦠 Chapter 2.2: Coevolution of Earth and Life

**PTO prompt:** Scientists think the pace of evolution increased, producing much more complex life (including humans) in the past billion years, as a result of **oxygen increasing above a certain threshold**.

**Claim:** *Earth's systems and life coevolved over 3.5 billion years, resulting in the evolution of humans, with oxygen playing a central role.*

**Organisms that changed oxygen in Earth's spheres:**

- **Cyanobacteria** (photosynthesizing microbes) released oxygen into the **hydrosphere**, then the **atmosphere** (Great Oxidation Event, ~2.4 billion years ago).
- **Land plants** spread across the continents (from ~470 million years ago), adding oxygen to the atmosphere and building soil in the **geosphere**.
- **Ocean algae and plankton** still produce about half of the oxygen made by photosynthesis today.

**Times an oxygen change led to more complex life:**

- After the Great Oxidation Event → **eukaryotes** (complex cells) appear (~1.85 billion years ago).
- Oxygen rises again (~800–540 million years ago) → **Ediacara biota** and the **Cambrian explosion** of animals.
- Very high oxygen (~300 million years ago) → **giant insects** and large animals spread on land.

📖 Review the chapter: [Coevolution of Earth and Life](unit2-coevolution.qmd)
:::

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Origin of the Universe

::: {.evidence-box}
### 💥 Chapter 2.3: Origin of the Universe

**PTO prompt: Could life-supporting conditions exist elsewhere?** The universe started as one hot, dense state and expanded in every direction, and the processes that formed galaxies and solar systems were the same everywhere. So scientists think it is likely that other Earth-like planets exist.

**Claim:** *The way the universe has formed resulted in a universe with similar stars and galaxies throughout.*

**Evidence for the expansion of the universe (big bang theory):**

- **Redshift:** light from distant galaxies is stretched toward red. The farther the galaxy, the faster it is moving away (Hubble's law).
- **Cosmic microwave background (CMB):** faint microwave radiation from every direction, the leftover glow of the early hot universe (about 2.7 K today).
- **Hydrogen and helium:** the universe is about 75% hydrogen and 25% helium by mass, the ratio the big bang theory predicts.

**Evidence that stars and planets are similar throughout the universe:**

- **Spectra** of distant stars and galaxies show the **same elements** with the same spectral lines as the Sun, so the same physics works everywhere.
- Astronomers have confirmed **more than 5,000 exoplanets**, and many stars host planets, including rocky planets in their habitable zones.

📖 Review the chapter: [Origin of the Universe](unit2-big-bang.qmd)
:::

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: Origin of the Universe explanation + Reflection (pp. 13–14)

In your explanation, include:

1. Evidence that supports the **expansion of the universe** (the big bang theory)
2. Evidence that supports **stars and planets being similar** throughout the universe
3. Your **scientific reasoning** linking the evidence to the claim

**Reflection:** describe the concept/reasoning for each piece of evidence. Then answer: *Given that stars and solar systems throughout the universe are similar to ours, **how likely is it that one of them has intelligent life?***
:::

    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Hubble's law (redshift increasing with distance) is exactly what you'd see if all of space is expanding. Every observer, in any galaxy, would see the same pattern."
  }
])
```

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Asteroid Orbits

::: {.evidence-box}
### ☄️ Chapter 2.4: Asteroid Orbits

**PTO prompt:** To communicate with other intelligent life, a civilization must **exist long enough** to develop that technology. Asteroid impacts can wipe out species, possibly ending a civilization first. But an advanced society could use a **gravity tractor** to redirect an asteroid headed for its planet.

**Claim:** *Scientists can pinpoint where an asteroid is and will be, and then use a gravity tractor to deflect it.*

**Key evidence:**

- **Predicting position:** telescopes measure an asteroid's position over many nights. **Kepler's laws** and **Newton's law of gravity** then predict its orbit years ahead. Example: Apophis (average distance ≈ 0.92 AU, period ≈ 0.89 years) will pass about 32,000 km from Earth's surface on April 13, 2029, closer than geostationary satellites.
- **Gravity tractor:** a spacecraft **hovers** near the asteroid without touching it. Their **mutual gravity** pulls the asteroid very gently toward the spacecraft, and the craft's thrusters keep it in place. Over years, this tiny tug changes the asteroid's speed and shifts its orbit so it misses.
- **Deflection is possible:** NASA's **DART** mission (2022) crashed into the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos and shortened its orbit by about 32 minutes. That proved we can change an asteroid's path. The gravity tractor is a slower, more precise method that has not been flown yet.

📖 Review the chapter: [Asteroid Orbits](unit2-asteroids.qmd)
:::

### 🛰️ Gravity Tractor Calculator

The tug on the asteroid depends only on the **spacecraft's mass** and **how close it hovers**: $a = \dfrac{G\,m_{\text{craft}}}{d^2}$. A small change in speed, applied **years ahead**, grows into a big shift in where the asteroid ends up.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gtMass = Inputs.range([1, 40], {label: "Spacecraft mass (metric tons):", step: 1, value: 20})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gtDist = Inputs.range([100, 500], {label: "Hover distance from asteroid's center (m):", step: 10, value: 200})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gtTow = Inputs.range([0.5, 10], {label: "Towing time (years):", step: 0.5, value: 1})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gtLead = Inputs.range([1, 30], {label: "Warning time after towing (years):", step: 1, value: 10})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const G = 6.674e-11, yr = 3.156e7, earthR = 6371;
  const acc = G * gtMass * 1000 / (gtDist * gtDist);    // m/s^2
  const dv = acc * gtTow * yr;                            // m/s
  const shiftKm = 3 * dv * gtLead * yr / 1000;            // along-track drift approximation
  const pct = shiftKm / earthR;
  const W = 360, H = 150;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "560px").style("height", "auto").style("display", "block").style("margin", "8px auto");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 12).attr("fill", "#0a0a2e");
  const barMax = 300, scaleKm = barMax / (2 * earthR);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 30).attr("y", 30).attr("fill", "#dfe6e9").attr("font-size", 11).text("Shift in where the asteroid arrives vs. Earth's radius");
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 30).attr("y", 50).attr("width", earthR * scaleKm).attr("height", 22).attr("fill", "#0984e3").attr("rx", 4);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 36).attr("y", 66).attr("fill", "white").attr("font-size", 10).text("Earth's radius 6,371 km");
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 30).attr("y", 85).attr("width", Math.max(2, Math.min(barMax, shiftKm * scaleKm))).attr("height", 22).attr("fill", pct >= 1 ? "#00b894" : "#e17055").attr("rx", 4);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 36).attr("y", 101).attr("fill", "white").attr("font-size", 10).text(`Shift ≈ ${Math.round(shiftKm).toLocaleString()} km${shiftKm * scaleKm > barMax ? " (off scale)" : ""}`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 30).attr("y", 132).attr("fill", pct >= 1 ? "#55efc4" : "#fab1a0").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .text(pct >= 1 ? "✅ Enough to move a direct hit off the Earth" : "⚠️ Not enough on its own: tow longer or start earlier");
  return html`<div>
    <div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px;justify-content:center;margin:8px 0;">
      <div style="background:#f5f3ff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:10px;padding:10px 14px;min-width:150px;text-align:center;"><div style="font-size:.8em;">Pull on asteroid</div><b>${acc.toExponential(1)} m/s²</b></div>
      <div style="background:#f5f3ff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:10px;padding:10px 14px;min-width:150px;text-align:center;"><div style="font-size:.8em;">Speed change</div><b>${(dv * 1000).toFixed(2)} mm/s</b></div>
      <div style="background:#f5f3ff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:10px;padding:10px 14px;min-width:150px;text-align:center;"><div style="font-size:.8em;">Shift at Earth</div><b>${Math.round(shiftKm).toLocaleString()} km</b></div>
    </div>
    ${svg.node()}
    <div style="font-size:.8em;color:#718096;text-align:center;">Simplified model: shift ≈ 3 × (speed change) × (warning time), the rule of thumb for a small change along the orbit. Real missions only need to steer the asteroid away from a small "keyhole," which takes much less.</div>
  </div>`;
}
```

# Unit Closing Task: Construct and Defend an Argument

::: {.engage-box}
## 👽 Why haven't we found life outside Earth?

In **1961**, a scientist named **Frank Drake** created an equation to predict the likelihood of intelligent life, capable of communicating with humans on Earth, existing on other planets in the Milky Way.

This equation **cannot be solved definitively**, because scientists do not yet know what numbers to assign to each factor.

**Your task:** Given this equation and everything you have learned in this unit, construct an argument about **whether or not it is likely that there is intelligent life somewhere else in the Milky Way or in the Universe**, and **whether or not we will make contact with it.**
:::

## The Drake Equation

$$N = R_* \times f_p \times n_e \times f_l \times f_i \times f_c \times L$$

| Factor | Meaning (from your PTO) |
|---|---|
| $N$ | The **number** of civilizations in the Milky Way Galaxy with which communication might be possible |
| $R_*$ | The **rate** of formation of stars in the galaxy (stars per year) |
| $f_p$ | The fraction of those stars with **planetary** systems |
| $n_e$ | The number of planets per solar system with an **environment** suitable for life |
| $f_l$ | The fraction of suitable planets on which **life** actually appears |
| $f_i$ | The fraction of life-bearing planets on which **intelligent** life emerges |
| $f_c$ | The fraction of those planets with intelligent life that develop interstellar **communication** |
| $L$ | The **length** of time such civilizations release detectable signals into space (years) |

Pick a starting set of values, then adjust each slider to match **your** evidence-based estimate.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
drakePresets = ({
  "Middle-of-the-road": {R: 2, fp: 1, ne: 0.2, fl: 0.1, fi: 0.01, fc: 0.1, L: 10000},
  "Optimistic": {R: 3, fp: 1, ne: 0.5, fl: 1, fi: 0.5, fc: 0.5, L: 1000000},
  "Pessimistic": {R: 1.5, fp: 0.9, ne: 0.1, fl: 0.001, fi: 0.001, fc: 0.01, L: 1000}
})
```

```{ojs}

```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof drake = {
  const p = drakePresets[drakePreset];
  return Inputs.form({
    R: Inputs.range([0.5, 10], {label: "R* — new stars per year", step: 0.5, value: p.R}),
    fp: Inputs.range([0.05, 1], {label: "fp — fraction with planets", step: 0.05, value: p.fp}),
    ne: Inputs.range([0.01, 2], {label: "ne — suitable planets per system", step: 0.01, value: p.ne}),
    fl: Inputs.range([0.0001, 1], {label: "fl — fraction where life appears", value: p.fl, transform: Math.log}),
    fi: Inputs.range([0.0001, 1], {label: "fi — fraction with intelligent life", value: p.fi, transform: Math.log}),
    fc: Inputs.range([0.0001, 1], {label: "fc — fraction that communicate", value: p.fc, transform: Math.log}),
    L: Inputs.range([100, 100000000], {label: "L — years signals last", value: p.L, transform: Math.log})
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
drakeSteps = {
  const v = drake;
  const steps = [
    {step: "R*: stars formed per year", val: v.R},
    {step: "× fp: with planets", val: v.R * v.fp},
    {step: "× ne: suitable environment", val: v.R * v.fp * v.ne},
    {step: "× fl: life appears", val: v.R * v.fp * v.ne * v.fl},
    {step: "× fi: intelligent life", val: v.R * v.fp * v.ne * v.fl * v.fi},
    {step: "× fc: communicates", val: v.R * v.fp * v.ne * v.fl * v.fi * v.fc},
    {step: "× L: N (civilizations now)", val: v.R * v.fp * v.ne * v.fl * v.fi * v.fc * v.L}
  ];
  return steps;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const N = drakeSteps[drakeSteps.length - 1].val;

  const verdict = N < 1 ? "Less than 1: we may be the only communicating civilization in the Milky Way right now."
    : N < 10 ? `About ${Math.round(N)} communicating civilization(s) in the Milky Way right now.`
    : N < 10000 ? `About ${Math.round(N).toLocaleString()} communicating civilizations in the Milky Way.`
    : `${Math.round(N).toLocaleString()} civilizations: the galaxy should be buzzing. So where is everybody? (the Fermi paradox)`;
  return html`<div style="padding:20px;border-radius:15px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#00a8a5,#6c5ce7);color:white;text-align:center;margin:10px 0;">
    <div style="font-size:1em;">N = R* × fp × ne × fl × fi × fc × L</div>
    <div style="font-size:2.4em;font-weight:800;margin:8px 0;font-family:'Space Grotesk',sans-serif;">N ≈ ${fmt(N)}</div>
    <div style="font-weight:700;">${verdict}</div>
  </div>`;
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Which factors do we know?

We know the first factors fairly well: the Milky Way makes a few new stars each year, and most stars have planets. The later factors ($f_l$, $f_i$, $f_c$, $L$) are **almost completely unknown**. Earth is our only example. Your unit evidence is what lets you make **informed** estimates and defend them.
:::

    correct: 1,
    explanation: "N is a product, so multiplying any factor by k multiplies N by k. Doubling R* doubles N, but making L 100× longer multiplies N by 100."

    q: "Why can't the Drake equation be solved definitively?",
    options: ["It has a math error", "Scientists don't yet know what numbers to assign to several factors, like fi, fc, and L", "It only works for the Sun", "It was written before computers"],
    correct: 1,

  }
])

## What Your Argument Must Consider

Your PTO lists six points. Each one matches part of the Drake equation and a chapter from this unit.

| Consider the likelihood of... | Drake factor | Evidence from |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Stars with planetary systems similar to Earth | $R_*$, $f_p$ | [Origin of the Universe](#revisiting-the-performance-task-origin-of-the-universe) |
| 2. Other planets being stable enough to support life | $n_e$ | [Stability of the Solar System](#revisiting-the-performance-task-stability-of-the-solar-system) |
| 3. Other planets having the right conditions to produce life and sustain evolution | $n_e$, $f_l$ | [Coevolution of Earth and Life](#revisiting-the-performance-task-coevolution-of-earth-and-life) |
| 4. Evolution occurring long enough to produce intelligent life | $f_i$ | [Coevolution](#revisiting-the-performance-task-coevolution-of-earth-and-life), [Opening: Tell the Story](unit2-opening.qmd#tell-the-story-evolution-of-life-on-earth) |
| 5. Societies surviving long enough to develop interstellar communication | $f_c$, $L$ | [Asteroid Orbits](#revisiting-the-performance-task-asteroid-orbits) |
| 6. Those societies overlapping with ours so our signals are detectable to each other | $L$ | [Asteroid Orbits](#revisiting-the-performance-task-asteroid-orbits), the Drake equation |

# Unit Summary

| Big idea | What the evidence shows |
|---|---|
| **It took ~4.5 billion years** | Life appeared early but stayed single-celled for billions of years; humans appeared only ~300,000 years ago |
| **Stability of the Solar System** | The late heavy bombardment (~4.1–3.8 billion years ago) likely delayed life until ~3.5 billion years ago |
| **Coevolution of Earth and Life** | Life added oxygen to Earth's systems; oxygen passing thresholds allowed complex cells, animals, and eventually humans |
| **Five mass extinctions** | Wiped out 70–95% of species each time, yet opened space for new groups (mammals after K-T) |
| **Origin of the Universe** | Redshift, CMB, and H/He abundance support the big bang; spectra show the same elements everywhere, so Earth-like planets are likely |
| **Asteroid Orbits** | Orbits are predictable with Kepler's and Newton's laws; a gravity tractor could deflect a threatening asteroid |
| **Drake equation** | $N = R_* f_p n_e f_l f_i f_c L$; the later factors are unknown, so the answer depends on evidence-based estimates |

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildUnit2Quiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#00a8a5 0%,#6c5ce7 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.85;margin-top:4px;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #c7d2fe;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#f8f9ff;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => {
          b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null;
          b.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0"; b.style.background="#f8fafc"; b.style.color="#475569";
        });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";btn.style.color="#276749";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";btn.style.color="#9b2c2c";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          const correctBtn = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
          correctBtn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";correctBtn.style.background="#f0fff4";correctBtn.style.color="#276749";correctBtn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";fb.style.borderRadius="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```
